questions.stem: On what date was NITI Aayog established, replacing the Planning Commission?
questions.explanation: The NITI (National Institution for Transforming India) Aayog was established on 1 January 2015 via a Union Cabinet resolution, replacing the 65-year-old Planning Commission (1950–2014). Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog was created NOT by an Act of Parliament — it is an executive body, making it easier to restructure but also legally weaker.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a component of NITI Aayog's structure?

options.option_text: Governing Council (Chief Ministers of States + Lt Governors of UTs)

questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's structure: (1) Chairperson — PM; (2) Vice Chairperson — appointed by PM; (3) Full-time members; (4) Part-time members (max 2, from universities/research bodies); (5) Ex-officio members (max 4 Union Ministers); (6) Governing Council — CMs + LGs; (7) Regional Councils — for specific issues; (8) Special Invitees — experts nominated by PM; (9) CEO — Secretary-rank officer. There is NO legislative or elected component — it's wholly executive.

questions.stem: Which of the following distinguishes NITI Aayog from the erstwhile Planning Commission?

options.option_text: NITI Aayog has financial/budgetary allocation powers; Planning Commission did not
NITI Aayog is a 'think tank' WITHOUT fund-allocation powers; Planning Commission had fund-allocation powers
NITI Aayog is a constitutional body; Planning Commission was statutory
NITI Aayog's Chairman is elected by Parliament; Planning Commission's was appointed by the President

questions.explanation: The biggest functional difference: the Planning Commission (1950–2014) had discretionary power to allocate central funds to States under Plan schemes. NITI Aayog explicitly has NO allocation powers — it is a think-tank, advising the Finance Ministry & the Cabinet. This removed a key source of Centre-State bargaining leverage from the Planning Commission era. Neither body was/is constitutional; both are executive creations. The PM chairs both.

questions.stem: Who was the first Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog?
questions.explanation: Arvind Panagariya (economist, Columbia University) was the first Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog (January 2015 – August 2017). He was succeeded by Rajiv Kumar (2017–22), and then Suman Bery (2022–present). Amitabh Kant served as CEO of NITI Aayog, NOT as Vice-Chairperson.

questions.stem: Which of the following indices is NOT published by NITI Aayog?

options.option_text: Health Index (State/UT ranking on health outcomes)
World Bank's Ease of Doing Business Index

questions.explanation: NITI Aayog publishes several ranking reports: SDG India Index, MPI-India, Health Index, School Education Quality Index, Composite Water Management Index, India Innovation Index, Export Preparedness Index. The Ease of Doing Business Index is published by the World Bank (it was discontinued in 2021, replaced by the B-READY project) — not NITI Aayog. Though NITI has a role in popularising DBR rankings domestically via DPIIT's Business Reform Action Plan.

questions.stem: Which among the following is a Constitutional Body and NOT a non-Constitutional/Statutory body?
questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is a CONSTITUTIONAL body — Article 280. NITI Aayog is non-constitutional, non-statutory (executive resolution only). CBI is non-constitutional; it is based on the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 — so it's a STATUTORY body. NHRC is a STATUTORY body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. Important categorisation for exams.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following bodies was part of the Planning Commission's structure but has NOT been carried over to NITI Aayog?

options.option_text: Programme Evaluation Organisation (PEO) — evaluates central schemes
The Planning Commission office in Yojana Bhavan (now NITI Bhawan)

questions.explanation: The National Development Council (NDC), chaired by the PM and including all CMs, was the highest body reviewing Five-Year Plans under the Planning Commission. NDC was NOT formally abolished, but it has been effectively replaced by NITI Aayog's Governing Council. The PEO continues under NITI's Development Monitoring & Evaluation Office. IAMR was renamed as NILERD (National Institute of Labour Economics Research & Development) in 2014 and continues.

questions.stem: The 'Aspirational Districts Programme' is run by which of the following bodies?
questions.explanation: The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP), launched in January 2018, is coordinated by NITI Aayog. It ranks 112 of India's most-backward districts on 49 KPIs across 5 sectors (Health & Nutrition, Education, Agriculture, Financial Inclusion & Skill Dev., Basic Infrastructure) and incentivises improvement. It is one of NITI Aayog's flagship governance initiatives. The Ministry of Rural Development's flagship is MGNREGA, not ADP.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a STATUTORY (not constitutional) body?

options.option_text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.explanation: SEBI was set up in 1988 as an administrative body; it became a STATUTORY body with the SEBI Act, 1992. UPSC (Article 315), CAG (Article 148), and ECI (Article 324) are all CONSTITUTIONAL bodies. Distinguishing statutory vs. constitutional is a common exam trap — statutory bodies are created by an Act of Parliament; constitutional bodies are named in the Constitution itself.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog's Governing Council: 1) It is the apex body of NITI Aayog. 2) All Chief Ministers + Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories with legislatures are members. 3) The Finance Minister of the Union is an ex-officio member. Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 CORRECT — the Governing Council IS the apex body of NITI Aayog. Statement 2 CORRECT — all CMs of States + LGs of UTs are members (UTs WITHOUT legislatures are represented by Administrators, but the classic composition is CMs + LGs). Statement 3 WRONG — Union Ministers are ex-officio members of NITI Aayog (not specifically the Governing Council in this way); the PM chairs the Governing Council with CMs/LGs as its members; Union Ministers attend as special invitees.
